findings.text: A family of hash-table acquisition helpers offers deduplicating access to inodes by filesystem plus caller-defined match or by number. When a match exists the existing object is returned with appropriate waiting and revalidation; otherwise a fresh object is hashed and handed back still marked new and locked so the caller can populate it, with spare allocations discarded on races.

Newly hashed objects enter I_NEW while locked, during which other acquirers wait and then revalidate for unhashed removal. I_CREATING supports exclusive establishment while I_FREEING and I_WILL_FREE cause waiting or skipping. Clearing of the new mark happens outside the viewed range, and state changes require the per-object lock.

Global hash-table mutation and lookup use inode_hash_lock, with per-object i_lock taken nested inside when marking state or linking. Read-side scans that avoid the hash lock require held read-side critical section protection and skip objects flagged as freeing. A separate private lock serializes the unique-number counter, and state assignment asserts i_lock is held.

Hash-table identity is scoped by filesystem instance combined with either caller-defined equivalence or inode number, so at most a single hashed object exists per identity. Concurrent insertion attempts converge on the pre-existing object rather than duplicating it, and number allocation verifies absence of collision before handing out a value.

Lightweight search helpers expose direct hash-chain matching without acquisition or reference-count semantics. Locked scanning evaluates a tri-state matcher under hash protection, while read-side variants require an active critical section and ignore objects undergoing teardown. Results are only stable under the associated protection.

A monotonic allocator supplies numbers that avoid a caller-provided reserved prefix and any value already present for the filesystem. It advances a shared counter under a private lock while verifying absence through a read-side hash scan.

Creation-time insertion routines attempt to hash a caller-provided object and report contention distinctly from success. They wait for freeing objects, reject concurrent establishing attempts, merge waiting for new objects, and retry when the conflicting object disappears, returning a busy indication when an established peer remains.
open_flags groups open-path intent as a small record carrying the user open mode, creation mode, derived access mode, intent code and lookup modifier.

xattr_name holds a bounded name buffer sized for the maximum allowed length plus terminator. kernel_xattr_ctx pairs user pointers for value exchange with a kernel buffer and length, plus a resolved name reference and control flags.

stashed_operations bundles three callbacks that manage a stashed dentry lifecycle: one to capture or replace the stashed reference, one to release associated data, and one to initialize a fresh inode from that data.

Special objects receive default operations selected by file kind, with device numbers recorded for device kinds and socket kinds left with no open handling; unrecognized kinds emit a diagnostic. Ownership setup derives user and group identity through namespace-aware mapping, inheriting the parent group and set-group bit when the parent carries it, with directories always preserving that bit.

Small attribute helpers delegate timestamp and modification marking with default or context-derived flags, report whether synchronous persistence is required for files or directories based on mount and inode flags, wait interruptibly for direct input-output completion, update masked flag bits with misuse detection, and constrain page-cache allocation to low memory.
Block mapping delegates to the address-space operation when present, translating the caller's logical position in place and reporting success, otherwise signaling lack of support.

The non-final put helper assumes the object is neither freeing nor cleared and retains at least another reference, warning if the decrement reaches zero. Diagnostic dumping uses fault-tolerant reads and falls back to placeholder identification when superblock or filesystem naming is unreadable. The trivial drop helper unconditionally requests disposal.
FIEMAP_MAX_EXTENTS defines the upper bound on extent descriptors transferable in a single mapping request, expressed as the maximum unsigned count divided by the descriptor size.

Extent reporting supports a counting mode when no destination capacity is offered and a storing mode otherwise, stopping when capacity fills or a terminal mark appears. Certain provider flags imply broader unknown, encoded or unaligned indications, and cleared descriptors are published to user memory. Preparation validates non-empty ranges against the filesystem maximum, trims overlong spans, rejects incompatible control flags while echoing them, and optionally flushes dirty data for synchronous requests.

Input-output control dispatch forwards generic commands to file operations while normalizing unknown-command signaling, gates block-number translation behind a raw-access privilege with range and overflow handling, validates mapping descriptor counts before invoking filesystem mapping and reflects results back, resolves clone sources through scoped descriptors with exact-length enforcement, and translates allocation requests with file-relative offset handling before delegating to allocation.

Range cloning requires both files to reside on the same filesystem, rejects directories and non-regular participants, enforces read access on the source and write access without append on the destination, verifies offsets and lengths for negativity and overflow plus permission and notification approval, fences the operation with write protection, and emits access and modification notifications on success.

Control paths that exchange structures with user memory treat copy failures as faults and validate user-supplied counts, offsets and whence selectors before acting. Overlarge block translations are clamped with rate-limited warnings, and mapping helpers propagate fault indications distinctly from completion signaling.
Access-control helpers in this configuration unconditionally report lack of support. Inode hash sizing is governed by a boot-time parameter parsed early and retained in static storage.
